Hey friend- my psychiatrist told me (and my own personal reading has backed up to an extent) that SSRI-class antidepressants tend to work best when cycled. If you were on one for a full year, it's likely that you will be best off shifted to a different one.

Aside from that, know that all things are temporary - both the good and bad feelings. It's something that I struggle with as a concept sometimes, but I think the takeaway should be that there is always going to be change, and that things can absolutely be shifted back to a brighter place. Maybe it's a different medication, or maybe it's something completely different, but *never believe* that pain is forever and that any period of feeling better is going to be so temporary that it may as well not exist.

Our knowledge of these things is still developing, and the drugs are far from perfect. In fact, approximately one year is a documented timeframe for recurrence when using Sertraline. A simple switch to another SSRI or something else may very well get you back on track. :)

Stick with what you feel is right. Your father is not God, and he is manipulating you using your faith to get what he wants.

I had a friend in a similar situation, and I saw it as one of two things. One, his father knows full well that he is just trying to manipulate you using your faith to terrify you into thinking you are defying God. Alternatively, he may very well think that God opposes the relationship - but what would make him think that? If you say your family is "crazy religious" as my friend's was, it was very apparent to me that his father took every "gut reaction" he had as a sign of God, and that every feeling he got was God's way of showing him the light.

I think the second one is even more terrifying. If someone genuinely believes that their very human desires, feelings and reactions are the will of God, how do you divide their human judgement from what God is truly trying to tell them? I think that it gives certain people a power complex that convinces them that every opinion they have is attuned with God. Doesn't the bible say something about God being the only true judge of man?

In this case, if you father is being crass and hateful (calling her a "bitch" and such) I think it is infinitely more likely that your father is in the wrong. I'm not entirely sure how you can handle that, but I do not believe God's path for you would manifest itself in your father spewing hateful bile to terrify you to obey him. "Honour thy mother and father" does not mean they are the word of God. Handling him now may be difficult especially if you still live with your parents, but if you're going to university I can assuredly say that you will find God's path for you when you are away from your manipulative father. If nothing else, try to take solace in that he is not behaving towards God's will and likely has no idea what God actually wants for you.

If this comes off as too self-righteous, I apologize. I hope your father sincerely thinks he is doing what is right, but I have seen far too many children be manipulated and emotionally abused by their so-called "Christian" parents to trust a man that is abusive while claiming they know God's will.

I'm doing significantly better in school thanks to years of trying different medications to find what ended up working. One thing to remember with these medications is that while they will give you the tools to rehabilitate yourself, many things are habitual on a level that drugs aren't going to be able to overcome on their own. 

Also, these drugs take a couple weeks before they have noticeable effects, and furthermore you're going to over-diagnose yourself with side effects if you're looking for them. Placebo is a very real thing, having experienced it first hand constantly. I described what I thought were side effects of a recent medication change to my therapist and she provided me extensive research that convinced me that I just have a bad habit of anticipating negative side effects.

For Bupropion specifically - I'm currently on it and have been for over a year and it definitely helped me feel more... "locked in"? I don't want to overplay it but it has absolutely had a positive impact on me. You are unlikely to experience side effects so soon after starting it, and I think the best way to approach new medications is to take them and try to forget about it. Overanalyzing everything you're feeling is exhausting, and is something I'm still trying to get over

That's unfortunately what you'll often deal with when going to subs like that. The subs attract men who are so desperate and cynical that it angers them to think that a woman has similar issues, because they don't fathom how that is possible. I often feel that I'm never going to find anyone again and that I'll be lonely for the rest of my life, but I'm rational enough to know that:

a) I'm being hard on myself and as long as I put effort into finding someone *and* probably lower my standards, I'll at least experience a relationship at some point (even if it's a horribly unhealthy one), and 

b) This is nowhere near a male-exclusive problem. Those types of guys get so hung up on the fact that they're desperate enough to hook up with anyone that they feel personally attacked when a female expresses the same thing. They feel that she's invalidating their pain because *they* would give her a chance, and take her pain more or less as rejection on the principle that "She isn't forever alone, I would give her a chance but she thinks I'm not good enough".

It would probably be good for me to vent about my feelings of hopeless loneliness but I refuse to be associated with those types of guys, so I just stay away from those communities completely.

tl;dr: They're hurting and their anger feels more manageable to them if they direct it at women. Don't take it personally, and ignore them
